_readme: Seed content for Elphyn. The tender_deck came from the Pigeon Ops decks Mason already reviewed (Oct 2026). Everything marked placeholder was written by Claude for the Zoo for Two prototype: keep, rewrite, or delete in your own words before Claire sees it. Claire adding her own hypotheticals and missions is the real deck.

missions.text: Make them laugh within the first 60 seconds.
Get them to share an elephant fact.
Get them to make a chicken noise.
Get them to name a bird that isn't a pigeon, crow, or seagull.
Plan a fake date where you're your animals: a turtle and a chicken.
Answer their next hypothetical with a number, a name, and an exact time.
Ask them a hypothetical before they can ask you one.
Get them to answer one of your hypotheticals more specifically than you would.
Get them to decide whether they're more chicken or elephant today, with three reasons.
Get them to rule whether you're more turtle or dog today, with three reasons.
Get them to do an elephant impression.
Get them to say one thing they're proud of this week.
Get them to compliment themselves without adding "I guess."
Give them a compliment so specific they ask how you noticed.
Get them to find a real bird outside and describe it to you.
Be a turtle for the whole call: everything slow. Don't break until they ask.
Get them to do a chicken walk on camera.
Read them three lines of something you wrote.
Get them to say the word “pineapple” without asking them to.
Work the phrase “as the prophecy foretold” into the conversation naturally.
Make three animal noises during the call, each disguised as a cough, sneeze, or laugh.
Convince them you adopted a pet goose named Gerald. Stay in character for three minutes.
Use the word “consequently” five times.
Find out their favorite cheese without asking anything about cheese.
Answer every question with another question for two straight minutes.
Hum the same song three times until they start humming it too.
Slip a fake fun fact into the conversation and see if they believe it.
Get them to say “I love you” first, without asking for it.
Compliment them three times, each more specific than the last, without them noticing a pattern.
Mention a made-up celebrity as if everyone knows who they are.
Mirror their posture on video for five minutes.
Get them to recommend you a movie, then act like you’ve already seen it and loved it.
Say “indubitably” at least twice.
Make them laugh within the first thirty seconds.
Bring up penguins three separate times, each in a different context.
Convince them you’ve taken up competitive yodeling.
Get them to agree to a dance-off the next time you’re together.
Narrate one moment of the call in a nature-documentary voice without breaking.
Get them to name a pet you’ll have someday.
Use a different accent for exactly one sentence, then never acknowledge it.
Start a sentence, pause dramatically for five seconds, then finish it like nothing happened.
Get them to describe the view from their window in detail.
Declare that today is a made-up national day and get them to celebrate it.
Get them to rate three random things out of ten, then reveal it was a personality quiz.
Get them to say their animal of the day without asking “what animal are you?”
Wear a hat on video and act like it’s completely normal.
Have a stuffed animal silently appear in the background and move it between shots.
Get them to sing one line of any song.
Agree with everything they say for two minutes, enthusiastically.
Use three words you’ve never said out loud before.
Describe your day as an epic quest for one full minute.
Get them to tell you a childhood memory you’ve never heard.
Convince them you can hear the ocean from where you are.
Review your last meal like a very serious food critic.
Say “plot twist” before two completely unremarkable statements.
End the call by granting them an official title, like Duchess of Snacks.
Get them to make a promise about something completely silly.
Tell them you’re proud of them for something specific, without it sounding planned.
Narrate one small thing you’re doing in the third person.
Get them to try a tongue twister.
End the call on a cliffhanger story you’ll finish next time.
Count how many times they say “like.” Reveal the number only at the end.
Slip in a compliment in a language you barely speak.
Act mildly scandalized by something mundane they mention, like their sock color.
Plan an imaginary vacation together in under two minutes.
Use the word “flabbergasted” correctly.
Treat your phone like a walkie-talkie for one exchange. Over.
Get them to describe their perfect sandwich in detail.

hypotheticals_dice.source: placeholder (Claude, Zoo prototype); a backup for when nobody has one, never a replacement for hers
items: If we were both animals at the same zoo, which enclosure would we escape from first, and how?
You can mail me exactly one smell. Which one, and how do you package it?
If your stuffed animal came to life for 24 hours, what’s the first thing it would complain about?
You wake up as a chicken who still has to attend all your classes today. Who notices first?
If our relationship were a restaurant, what’s on the menu, and what does the one-star review say?
You have to replace one of my bones with a household object. Which bone, which object?
If you could only communicate through interpretive dance for a week, what would “I miss you” look like?
A turtle and an elephant open a small business. What do they sell, and who handles customer service?
You get to rename one day of the week. What’s it called now, and what happens on it?
If I were a kitchen appliance, which one, and what’s my fatal flaw?
You can teleport, but only to places exactly 3,000 miles from where you’re standing. Where do you go first?
A pigeon steals your lunch. What’s your villain origin story?
Zombie apocalypse, right now, and all you have is what’s in your bag. What’s the plan?
You’re a ghost haunting a library. What do you rearrange, and why?
Which fruit would make the worst president, and what’s its first executive order?
If all the animals we’ve ever pretended to be had a group chat, what’s the most recent message?
You can add one rule to every airport in the world. What is it?
If you were a font, which one, and who keeps misusing you?
We’re two mice living in a museum. Which exhibit is home, and what’s our nightly route?
You wake up and every bird can talk, but only to you. What do they keep complaining about?
We get one time capsule to open in ten years. What goes in, and what does the note say?
A wizard turns you into a lamp for a day. Whose room are you in, and what do you witness?
What’s the most dramatic possible way to deliver a sandwich to me across the country?
If clouds had personalities, which kind of cloud are you, and what’s your problem?
You’re mayor of a town populated entirely by dogs. What’s your first big infrastructure project?
Describe me using only weather. What’s the forecast?
One object in your room becomes sentient. Which one, and what’s its first question?
We’re a duo in a heist movie. What are we stealing, and who messes up?
A genie grants three wishes, but each has to cost under five dollars. What do you pick?
You swap lives with any animal for a week. Which one, and what’s the hardest part?
If you were a cereal mascot, what’s the cereal and what’s your catchphrase?
You’re stuck in an elevator with a raccoon for two hours. How does it end?
If our love were measured in a weird unit, what’s the unit, and how many do we have?
For a month you can only eat foods of one color. Which color?
A tiny orchestra follows you for a day. Which moment needs the most dramatic music?
You get to invent a holiday just for us. What’s it called, and what are the traditions?
The moon has a customer service line. What do you complain about?
Which household chore would be an Olympic sport if you were the judge?
You have a tail for a day. What kind, and what does it give away about your feelings?
You’re a chef and I’m the food critic. What dish do you make to win me over?
We each get a sidekick animal. Which ones, and do they get along?
Write a strongly worded letter to a vegetable. Which vegetable, and what’s the first line?
You find a secret door in your room. Where does it lead?
You can talk to one historical figure, but only through charades. Who, and what do you try to ask?
You shrink to the size of a bee for one afternoon. Where do you go?
Which animal would be the most annoying roommate, and what’s its worst habit?
If our phone calls were a TV show, what’s the title, and what does the theme song sound like?
You get a free billboard for a week. What does it say?
If you were a dessert, what kind, and how do you react when someone eats you?
You can make it rain one thing that isn’t water for ten minutes. What falls?
If your life had a laugh track, which moment this week gets the biggest laugh?
A dragon moves in next door. How do you become friends?
You become fluent in one animal’s language. Which, and what’s the first conversation?
You get to rename three buildings on your campus. What are the new names?
If your laptop could talk, what would it beg you to stop doing?
You’re a penguin giving a TED talk. What’s the topic?
We build a blanket fort big enough to live in. What rooms does it have?
One button lets you skip one boring thing forever. What do you skip?
A snail becomes your personal assistant. How does your week go?
Which kitchen utensil best represents your personality today?
You’re an elephant who never forgets. What’s the most useless thing you remember?
You get dinner with any cartoon character. Who, and what do you order?
We swap hometowns for a year. What’s the first thing you do in mine?
You find a tiny door at the base of a tree. Who answers when you knock?
If your shadow had opinions, what would it say about you?
A turtle challenges you to a race and wins. How do you explain it to your friends?
You can only use three emoji for the rest of your life. Which three?
You’re a lighthouse. Who do you guide, and what do you think about all night?
Our relationship gets a mascot. What is it, and what’s its signature dance?
Any animal can be made the size of a house cat. Which one do you keep as a pet?
You’re a weather forecaster for feelings. What’s today’s report for you?
You get one superpower, but it only works on Tuesdays. What is it?
If our voicemails were museum exhibits, what would the plaque say?
You’re a sock that got lost in the dryer. Where did you actually go?
Every textbook gets one smell. Which smell for which subject?
You win a lifetime supply of something weird. What is it, and how do you use it?
If we were constellations, what shapes are we, and what’s the myth?
You’re a chicken running for class president. What’s your campaign slogan?
If the ocean could send one text, who would it text, and what would it say?
You can give the human body one upgrade. What is it?
Your favorite food goes on strike. What are its demands?
We’re trapped inside a board game. Which game, and who wins?
You can hear one person’s thoughts for one minute. Whose, and when?
A raccoon offers you a deal behind a dumpster. What’s the deal, and do you take it?
You can make one place on earth completely silent for an hour. Where?
You’re a houseplant. What do you want your owner to know?
You have to wear a costume to every class for a week. Which costume?
You choose the sound your phone makes when I text you. What is it?
A nature documentary narrator tells our love story. What’s the opening line?
A map shows treasure buried under your campus. What’s the treasure?
You can pass one law that only applies to cats. What is it?
You visit any fictional world as a background character. Which world, and what’s your job?
Time pauses for everyone but us for one hour. What do we do?
You’re a vending machine. What do you dispense, and what does it cost?
We raise a baby dinosaur together. What do we name it, and who’s the strict parent?
You can relive one ordinary day from this year. Which one?
I’m a turtle and you’re an elephant. Who carries who across the river, and how?
If you could put one thing from your city in my city, what would it be?
What would our two animals argue about on a long road trip?
You can hire a duck to follow you around and quack whenever someone lies. Do you hire it, and where do you take it first?
